images.note: Conjectural portrait (no life portrait of Penn exists); 1830-31 study, full-length version hangs at Independence NHP. Covers the Penn intro beat (admiral's son, Quaker, Tower of London). Later depiction, noted honestly.
images.title: William Penn at the Treaty Elm (study), Henry Inman, 1830-31

images.note: Title page of Penn's 1681 promotional pamphlet Some Account of the Province of Pennsilvania. Contemporary with the advertising beat (pamphlet across Europe, German edition).
images.title: Title page, Some Account of the Province of Pennsilvania, William Penn, 1681

images.note: 19th-century Quaker folk-art depiction of the Shackamaxon treaty tradition, NOT contemporary. Script explicitly hedges the meeting ('paintings came ninety years later'); image matches that hedge.
images.title: Penn's Treaty with the Indians, Edward Hicks, c.1840-44

images.alt_source: U.S. National Park Service (Germantown Friends' First Protest Against Slavery, 1688; courtesy Haverford College)
images.note: Page 1 of the 1688 Germantown Friends protest against slavery (Pastorius et al.). Contemporary manuscript; original held at Haverford College Quaker & Special Collections, this scan via LOC. Covers the anti-slavery protest beat.
images.source: Library of Congress, Rare Book & Special Collections
images.title: 1688 Germantown Friends' protest against slavery, page 1

images.note: 1918 reprint of Franklin's 1751 Observations Concerning the Increase of Mankind, open to the leaf bearing the exact 'Germanize us instead of our Anglifying them' passage quoted in the script. Later reprint of a contemporary text.
images.title: Franklin, Observations Concerning the Increase of Mankind (1751 text; 1918 reprint), 'Germanize us' passage

images.note: Title page of Saur's German-language almanac printed at Germantown, 1762/63. An almanac, not the newspaper Geschicht-Schreiber (1739); represents Saur's German-language press for the Pennsylvania Dutch beat.
images.title: Der Hoch-Deutsch Americanische Calender, Christopher Saur, Germantown, 1762/63

images.note: 1898 English translation of Gottlieb Mittelberger's 1756 Reise nach Pennsylvanien, whose account famously described the redemptioner system ('negotiated on the dock'). Later translation of a contemporary account.
images.title: Gottlieb Mittelberger, Journey to Pennsylvania (1756; 1898 English translation), title page
